title: Multidimensional revival dynamics in a bosonic many-body system
authors: Denis Ullmo, Steven Tomsovic, Gabriel M. Lando, Peter Schlagheck
abstract: The collapse and revival of localized states in many-body systems is a quintessential example of a quantum interference phenomenon that cannot be explained purely within mean-field theories. Historically, the majority of previous work on quantum revivals has been in a Schrödinger mechanics context, typically for effectively 1D systems with a focus on the autocorrelation function as the key detection observable. The general revival subject acquires a far greater complexity in the bosonic many-body context that offers a larger variety of observables and intrinsically implies high dimensionality. Here, the focus is on the simplest nontrivial (i.e., not 1D) bosonic many-body system, namely a symmetric two-site Bose-Hubbard model. The non-equilibrium situation of a coherent initial state prepared on one of the two sites of this integrable 2D system in the strongly self-trapping regime is considered. The revival behaviors emerging from the resulting dynamics within expectation values, coherences, and the autocorrelation function are theoretically derived, and the entanglement behavior is illustrated. Several new features, unknown so far in the Schrödinger context and identified here in terms of five ``puzzles'', are encountered and discussed, among them, a synchronized resurgence behavior, differing revivals times depending on the specific observable, and a manifestation of a precession that appears in the underlying mean field dynamics. These new phenomena can be entirely understood through a comprehensive semiclassical theory, building upon the underlying classical (mean-field) phase-space structure. A quantitative comparison of the latter with semiclassical predictions and quantum perturbative calculations yields an overall excellent agreement and confirms that a full semiclassical theory is pivotal for the understanding of these genuinely quantum many-body interference phenomena.
summary: This paper analyzes quantum revival dynamics in a two-site Bose-Hubbard model, a simple but non-trivial bosonic many-body system. It discovers several complex revival features not seen in 1D systems, such as synchronized resurgence. The key finding is that these phenomena are fully explained by developing and validating a comprehensive semiclassical theory.
main_problem: Investigating complex quantum revival dynamics in genuinely multidimensional bosonic many-body systems, moving beyond simple 1D models.
main_result: The study identifies new revival features, including synchronized resurgence and observable-dependent revival times, which are fully explained by a comprehensive semiclassical theory.
method: Theoretical derivation using semiclassical methods, quantum perturbation theory, and comparison against full quantum many-body dynamics.
model_or_system: The primary model is the symmetric two-site Bose-Hubbard model (a Bose-Hubbard dimer), which is integrable and serves as the simplest non-trivial bosonic many-body system.
key_observables: Expectation values, coherences, autocorrelation function, and entanglement behavior.
important_parameters: Strongly self-trapping regime, and the comparison between quantum and semiclassical limits.
main_assumptions: The system is assumed to remain integrable (like the two-site dimer); the semiclassical approach is an approximation valid for small inverse filling factor.
paper_structure: The paper reviews 1D revivals, focuses on the Bose-Hubbard dimer dynamics, and develops the theoretical framework by comparing semiclassical predictions with quantum perturbative and exact calculations.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding how quantum interference manifests in higher-dimensional, integrable bosonic systems, linking mean-field dynamics to genuine quantum effects.

Figure 2: Coherence on the initially populated site as a function of the scaled time τ = t/t0 rev (t0 rev = 2πℏ/U), calculated for Nα = 200 and γ = 0.14 (red line). As highlighted in the inset, the restoration of coherence at the revival time is nearly 99 percent. The zoomed panels highlight the first collapse of the recurrence oscillations (d,e), the first half-revival near τ = 0.5 (f,g), as well as the first full revival near τ = 1 (h,i).
